topic_summary: Analysis of the personhood boundary in abortion law, examining how different legal and philosophical traditions determine when moral and legal status begins, and how this determination structures rights, obligations, and state authority in reproductive contexts.

key_entities: State (authority claiming power to adjudicate personhood boundary)
Legal system (enforcement mechanism for personhood determinations)
key_tensions: Fetal moral status vs maternal autonomy (zero-sum rights allocation)
State authority to define personhood vs individual/community interpretive autonomy
Biological development continuum vs legal bright-line requirements

axes.structural_delta: Continuous biological development from conception through birth with no natural categorical boundaries
axes.primary_observable: Embryological development stages; organ formation timelines; viability thresholds
axes.selection_reason: Physical substrate providing the continuous developmental reality that all interpretive frameworks must address

axes.structural_delta: Competing readings of when moral/legal status begins, each instantiating different constraint structures
axes.primary_observable: Legal personhood definitions across jurisdictions; victim set composition in different frameworks; rights allocation patterns
axes.selection_reason: Central contested kernel with multiple structurally distinct readings; highest centrality score

axes.structural_delta: State's claimed authority to select one personhood reading and enforce it through criminal/civil law
axes.primary_observable: Criminal penalties for abortion; civil liability frameworks; enforcement mechanisms; jurisdictional variation
axes.selection_reason: Distinct observable (enforcement mechanisms vs personhood criteria); independent epsilon from kernel readings

axes.primary_observable: Viability determination protocols; gestational age cutoffs; medical exception frameworks
axes.selection_reason: Distinct coordination mechanism; different observable from both biological substrate and personhood readings

omegas.description: Indigenous traditions with distinct personhood frameworks (e.g., ensoulment at quickening, community-determined status) absent from analysis. Western legal/philosophical traditions dominate extraction.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + Absence Inventory

omegas.description: Prenatal testing and selective abortion create collision between reproductive autonomy and disability rights frameworks. Gradualist reading may mask eugenic extraction.
Advancing neonatal technology continuously lowers viability threshold, creating moving target for viability-based frameworks. Rope may become Snare as medical capability expands.
International human rights frameworks (ICCPR, CEDAW) provide competing interpretive authorities not addressed. State enforcement authority analysis limited to domestic context.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Four distinct axes with independent observables and epsilon values. Kernel structure properly identified with four readings. Dark matter probes surfaced four omega-level gaps.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The personhood boundary — the point at which moral and legal status begins — is a stabilized commitment that all parties argue about but read differently
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Competing interpretive authorities: religious traditions (natural law, divine ensoulment), philosophical frameworks (capacity-based, relational), legal positivism (state definition), medical profession (viability determination)

readings.commitment: Moral and legal personhood begins at conception/fertilization
readings.authority_grounding: Natural law / religious (Catholic, evangelical Protestant) / genetic uniqueness
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at conception; abortion becomes homicide; high suppression of alternative readings; state enforcement maximized

readings.commitment: Moral and legal personhood begins at viability (capacity for independent survival)
readings.authority_grounding: Medical profession / legal precedent (Roe framework) / capacity-based ethics
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at viability (~24 weeks); pre-viability abortion protected; medical profession gains gatekeeping authority; enforcement threshold technologically contingent

readings.commitment: Moral and legal personhood begins at birth
readings.authority_grounding: Legal positivism / autonomy frameworks / historical common law
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus not in victim set; pregnant person sole rights-holder; state enforcement minimized; abortion as healthcare decision

readings.commitment: Moral status develops gradually along developmental continuum; legal personhood requires bright-line but acknowledges arbitrariness
readings.authority_grounding: Philosophical ethics (gradualist theories) / pragmatic legal frameworks / developmental biology
readings.expected_structural_delta: Increasing moral weight through pregnancy; legal threshold pragmatically chosen; balancing frameworks rather than absolute rights; state interest increases with development

axiom_contradictions.basis: Conception reading's axiom (genetic uniqueness confers full moral status) requires rejecting birth reading's axiom (moral status requires independent existence). No single framework can hold both as true simultaneously.

Conception reading's axiom (personhood is binary and immediate at fertilization) requires rejecting gradualist reading's axiom (moral status develops incrementally). Binary vs continuous frameworks are mutually exclusive.
